page: Microsoft Azure E64a_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the EAv4 family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7452 processor operating at 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It also includes 1638 GB of bundled local storage and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core CPU performance measured by stress-ng falls in the bottom 10%, and LLM text generation for medium models is similarly positioned. However, multi-threaded capabilities are more robust, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and the PassMark CPU score ranking in the top 25%. Memory performance is also strong, as evidenced by the PassMark memory score, though uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths remain in the middle 50% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E64a_v4 offers high memory density and bundled local storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments for certain workloads. The primary tradeoff is the lower single-core execution speed, which makes it less suitable for single-threaded tasks. However, the high core count and substantial memory capacity provide a balanced resource density for multi-threaded applications.

This server configuration is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, multi-threaded data decompression, and enterprise applications requiring large memory footprints alongside local scratch storage. It is less suited for latency-sensitive single-threaded processing or large-scale LLM inference.
